posts.title: 1.9-million-year-old discovery rewrites human migration story
posts.dek: New dating places early humans in Jordan at least 1.9 million years ago, alongside Dmanisi in Georgia.

posts.title: Jordan Valley site pushes human arrival outside Africa back to 1.9 million years
posts.dek: New dating at 'Ubeidiya matches the age of Dmanisi in Georgia, suggesting multiple toolmaking groups left Africa at roughly the same time.

posts.title: Pottery cargo off Turkey may be oldest shipwreck ever found
posts.dek: A wreck near Kekova dated to roughly 2700–2400 BCE could push back the record by centuries. Only the jars survive, but their shapes and residues hint at a far-flung trade network.

posts.title: Postholes reveal a possible ceremonial hall beside 5,000-year-old royal tombs
posts.dek: Three timber buildings reconstructed from 120 postholes may have formed a ritual precinct alongside elite burials at Fanshan.

posts.title: how prehistoric communities survived a volcanic apocalypse
posts.dek: A massive eruption 7,300 years ago reshaped lives across Japan, but not all regions fared the same.

posts.title: Cut marks on mammoth bones suggest Ice Age hunters killed the giants at Breitenbach
posts.dek: New finds at Germany's largest Aurignacian open-air site challenge the idea that early humans only scavenged ancient ivory. The evidence points to active hunting 30,000 years ago.

posts.title: Cut marks on mammoth bones suggest Ice Age hunters killed the giants themselves
posts.dek: New finds at a 30,000-year-old open-air site challenge the idea that early humans only scavenged ancient ivory. Cut marks point to active hunting and butchery.

posts.title: A 13,800-year-old base camp in interior Alaska shows early Americans settling in for the long haul
posts.dek: At Shégˊ Xdaltthˊíˊ, archaeologists found a hearth, a possible dwelling, the hemisphere's oldest needles, and wolf-like canids that may have lived alongside people.

posts.title: 300,000-year-old tools found in portugal
posts.dek: More than 200 stone artefacts recovered from a riverside location in central portugal.

posts.title: submerged ice age coast reveals ancient aboriginal landscape
posts.dek: diving rangers uncovered stone tools near a former river and a freshwater spring, supporting the sea floor holds deep cultural layers.

posts.title: 300,000-year-old tools found exactly where they fell in portugal
posts.dek: Archaeologists uncovered more than 200 stone artefacts in their original context, pushing back the timeline of human presence in western Iberia.

posts.title: a miniature fish among the dead
posts.dek: A tiny stone lure placed in a grave 7,600 years ago rewrites the origins of fishing technology.

posts.title: Ancient Aboriginal landscape found beneath Australia's seas
posts.dek: Archaeologists have identified stone artefacts and landscape features beneath the waters of north-western Australia, revealing how Aboriginal communities lived on land now drowned by rising seas after the last Ice Age.

posts.title: Stone tools found beneath Australia's drowned coast
posts.dek: Archaeologists have identified submerged stone artefacts linked to a freshwater spring and a rocky hill in north-western Australia, revealing how Aboriginal communities used landscapes now under the sea.

posts.title: underwater discoveries reveal ancient aboriginal landscape
posts.dek: rising seas drowned more than two million square kilometres of australia's continental shelf, but the archaeological record survived beneath the waves.

posts.title: first adult erectus found 200,000 years early
posts.dek: A 2-million-year-old skull fragment reshapes the origin story of our genus.

posts.title: Melting ice in Norway's highest mountains reveals 6,000-year-old arrows and toys
posts.dek: Archaeologists are recovering prehistoric arrows, clothing, and children's toys from ice that has remained frozen for millennia. The finds are rewriting textbooks on Stone Age mountain use.

posts.title: Neanderthals may have turned birch bark glue into ancient wound medicine
posts.dek: Experiments recreating Neanderthal birch tar production show every sample stopped Staphylococcus aureus growth, suggesting the adhesive doubled as a natural antibiotic.

posts.title: Ten-thousand-year-old posts and boards rest twenty metres down in a German lake
posts.dek: Divers recovered worked timbers from Lake Arendsee that may be the oldest wooden structures yet found in Central Europe.

posts.title: Wooden posts and split boards rest 20 metres down in a German lake
posts.dek: Archaeologists recovered worked wood up to 10,500 years old from Lake Arendsee. The pieces may belong to structures built by hunter-gatherers millennia before farming arrived.

posts.title: Wooden posts and split boards survive 10,500 years beneath a German lake
posts.dek: Divers recovered worked timbers from 20 metres down in Lake Arendsee. The pieces show felling marks and could rewrite what we know about hunter-gatherer building.

posts.title: 10,500-year-old wooden posts found beneath german lake
posts.dek: Divers recovered split boards and a tall post from lake arendsee, where waterlogged conditions have preserved stone-age timbers rarely seen elsewhere.

posts.title: Mesolithic timbers survive 10,500 years beneath a German lake
posts.dek: Worked posts and split boards found 20 metres underwater could rewrite what we know about hunter-gatherer construction in Central Europe.

posts.title: The Scouts at Ostia: A New Way to Bring the Ancient City to Its Neighbours
posts.dek: Around Ostia Antica the ancient city is swallowed by modern housing. A pilot project with a Scout Group tests whether community archaeology can work where no clear heritage community exists.
posts.source: Il capitale culturale. Studies on the Value of Cultural Heritage

posts.title: When the Neighbors Are the Community
posts.dek: A Scout Group steps into the role of heritage community at one of Rome's most urbanized archaeological sites, testing whether the concept can survive contact with a modern city.
posts.source: Il capitale culturale. Studies on the Value of Cultural Heritage

posts.title: A Scout Group as a Heritage Community
posts.dek: In one of Rome's most urbanized districts, a pilot project with a Scout Group tests whether community archaeology can work where no clear heritage community exists.
posts.source: Il capitale culturale. Studies on the Value of Cultural Heritage

posts.title: The shell that sent Lady 56 across medieval Europe
posts.dek: Ancient DNA separates the living from the dead at several medieval Swedish cemeteries. The burials were less about family ties, and more about community, custom, and possibly pilgrimage.

posts.title: The oldest complex cells were already choosing oxygen
posts.dek: More than 12,000 fossils from Australia link the earliest known eukaryotes to oxygenated seafloors between 1.7 and 1.4 billion years ago.

posts.title: A pyramid tomb where two worlds said goodbye
posts.dek: In Egypt's Western Desert, a small Roman-era pyramid tomb pairs hieroglyphic spells with a 19-line Greek poem for a man named Bisichthes.
